memos.headline: Relative strength bifurcation: GOOGL and CAT lead, MSFT/NVDA/PG lag badly
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market within our universe as of 12-Dec-2025. GOOGL (+75.6% over 26w, +19.8% 12w rel strength vs SPY) and CAT (+67.0% over 26w, +25.1% 12w rel strength) are the standout momentum leaders, both sitting within ~4% of 52-week highs with RSIs in the mid-to-high 50s—strong but not yet overbought. On the other side, MSFT (RSI 41.5, -5.2% vs 50d, -8.8% 12w rel strength), NVDA (RSI 39.9, -15.5% drawdown, -7.8% 4w rel strength), and PG (RSI 42.9, -19.0% drawdown, -12.1% 12w rel strength) are all breaking down below their 50-day means and underperforming SPY on every timeframe. I have highest conviction in the leaders and in avoiding PG, which is in a clear intermediate downtrend below both moving averages; I'd reconsider PG only on a reclaim above its 200d mean (~$158). AAPL and JPM sit in a comfortable middle ground—near highs, positive trend, but without the explosive relative strength of the top tier.

views.note: Parabolic 26w move of +75.6%, +48% above 200d mean, and dominant 12w rel strength of +19.8% vs SPY; would reassess on a close below 290 (~6% lower).
Massive +67% 26w gain, +42% above 200d mean, +25% 12w rel strength vs SPY, RSI 58.5 not yet stretched; invalidation below 550.
Steady uptrend with +17% 12w return, only -2.8% from highs, +14% 12w rel strength; low ATR of 1.59% keeps risk manageable; would cut below 260.
Sitting just -0.6% from 52w high with RSI 58.4 and positive trend vs both moving averages, but 12w rel strength is flat at -1.3%; needs a breakout above 320 to get more excited.
Near highs (-0.8% drawdown) and above both MAs, but flat 4w return and slightly negative 4w rel strength suggest consolidation rather than breakout.
Trading -5.2% below 50d mean with RSI 41.5 and -8.8% 12w rel strength vs SPY; downtrend intact until price reclaims ~$505 (50d area).
RSI 39.9 approaching oversold, -15.5% drawdown, -6.3% below 50d mean, and negative rel strength on all short-term frames; would reconsider on a close back above 190.
Worst in the universe: -19% drawdown, -9.5% below 200d mean, -12.1% 12w rel strength—clear intermediate downtrend with no sign of stabilization.
Bouncing short-term (+3.3% 1w) but still -43% from 52w high and below 200d mean; too early to call a reversal, need to see sustained closes above 360.
Middling setup: -10.9% drawdown, RSI 44.8, negative 4w and 12w rel strength, but still above 200d mean; watching 220 as support—a break below shifts to avoid.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Durable Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I see the strongest fundamental setups in NVDA and GOOGL this quarter. NVDA posted $57B in quarterly revenue (+62.5% YoY) with a 56% net margin and only $8.5B in total debt—this is extraordinary earnings power with minimal leverage. GOOGL delivered $102B in revenue (+15.9% YoY) at a 34.2% net margin on just $14.8B of debt, demonstrating operating leverage across its cloud and advertising segments. On the other side, UNH's net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on $113B of revenue, compressing net margin to just 2.1% while carrying $80B in debt—I need to see margin stabilization before getting constructive. XOM's revenue declined 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3%, reflecting commodity headwinds that could persist; the 8.8% net margin leaves little cushion. MSFT remains solid at 35.7% net margin and 18.4% revenue growth, though I note net income growth of 12.5% lagged the top line, suggesting rising costs that bear monitoring.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, and only $8.5B debt make this the cleanest earnings-power story in the universe; a sustained margin decline below 45% would change my view.
15.9% revenue growth with 34.2% net margin and low leverage ($14.8B debt) signals durable, high-quality earnings; I'd reassess if ad revenue growth decelerates below 10%.
18.4% revenue growth and 35.7% net margin are strong, but net income growth of only 12.5% suggests cost pressures from AI capex that I want to track in the next quarter.
Revenue of $180B (+13.4% YoY) with net margin expanding to 11.8% and net income up 38.2% shows operating leverage kicking in, though $55B in debt warrants attention.
Net income down 61.2% YoY to $2.35B with a 2.1% net margin on $80B of debt is cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for; I need margin recovery above 4% to reconsider.
Revenue down 5.2% and net income down 12.3% with an 8.8% net margin reflect commodity cyclicality; I'd need revenue stabilization and margin above 10% to turn constructive.

7.9% revenue growth and 26.8% net margin are solid but $90.7B in total debt is the highest in the universe ex-JPM, and the 86.4% net income jump likely reflects a tough prior-year comp rather than a new run-rate.
Revenue grew 9.5% but net income fell 6.7% YoY, compressing margin to 13%; I want to see cost discipline restore earnings growth before getting constructive.
8.8% revenue growth and 31% net margin are respectable for a bank, but the rate cycle outlook introduces uncertainty around NII durability.
3% revenue growth is sluggish even for a staple, though 21.2% net margin and 20% net income growth show mix/pricing discipline; I'd need top-line acceleration to get excited.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Meets Sticky Inflation and Rising Unemployment — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Cautious on Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has dropped 100bp over the past year to 3.75%, with 75bp of that in the last three months alone. However, CPI is running at 3.0% YoY as of September, which is uncomfortably above target, while unemployment has crept up to 4.50% (+30bp YoY), signaling a softening labor market that justifies continued cuts but limits how far the Fed can go. The 10y-2y spread has re-steepened sharply to +0.62pp from +0.11pp a year ago, confirming the market is pricing a sustained easing path with longer-term inflation risk. I have conviction that this late-cycle easing backdrop favors high-quality duration-sensitive growth names and defensive staples over cyclicals and energy; a CPI print re-accelerating above 3.5% or unemployment reversing below 4.2% would force me to reconsider the regime call.

views.note: Premium duration-sensitive growth benefits directly from falling front-end rates and a steepening curve in a late-cycle easing regime.
Quality mega-cap growth with strong cash flows is well-positioned as the Fed continues easing and the long end stays contained at 4.19%.
High-duration secular growth name benefits from rate cuts, though elevated CPI at 3% YoY introduces some valuation risk if inflation re-accelerates.
Defensive staple with pricing power is attractive as unemployment rises to 4.5% and the labor market softens, signaling late-cycle caution.
Steepening curve (+51bp YoY in 10y-2y spread) supports NIM expansion, but rising unemployment and slowing economy raise credit loss concerns.
Rising unemployment and late-cycle easing signal weakening industrial demand; cyclicals face headwinds as the labor market deteriorates.
Softening macro backdrop with rising unemployment suggests weakening demand for energy; easing cycle historically pressures commodity prices.
Consumer-facing tech giant benefits from lower rates supporting consumer spending and valuation multiples in an easing regime.
Benefits from rate cuts like other growth names but ad revenue sensitivity to economic slowdown tempers conviction given rising unemployment.
Defensive healthcare name is relatively insulated from rate moves, but macro regime offers no strong catalyst in either direction.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: AMZN and CAT Surged, MSFT and NVDA Sold Off — Narrative Shifts Now Six Weeks Old
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions and subsequent 8-K filing cadence across the universe to gauge where sentiment momentum may still have legs versus where it has been fully absorbed. AMZN (+9.6%) and CAT (+11.6%) posted the strongest positive earnings-day reactions in late October, signaling a decisive upward tone shift; however, these moves are now six weeks old and likely priced. MSFT (-2.9%) and NVDA (-3.2%) saw negative post-earnings reactions, and both have since filed governance-related 8-Ks (MSFT director changes, NVDA no follow-up catalyst), suggesting the negative narrative has not been offset by fresh positive catalysts. UNH has had an unusually high volume of filings — earnings, Reg FD, bylaws amendment, and a director departure — which I read as elevated organizational noise that could keep sentiment cautious. I have the most conviction on avoiding NVDA and MSFT near-term given their negative earnings reactions and absence of positive narrative shifts since, while AMZN's strong beat is likely already in the price.

views.note: The +9.6% earnings pop was decisive but is now six weeks stale with only a routine 'Other Events' filing since — upside sentiment likely priced.
An impressive +11.6% earnings reaction, but with no subsequent filings to sustain the narrative, the tone boost is likely fully absorbed.
Post-earnings sell-off of -3.2% with no positive follow-up catalyst filed since mid-November leaves negative sentiment as the prevailing tone.
The -2.9% earnings reaction was the worst among mega-cap tech peers, and the Dec 8 governance filing does nothing to shift the negative tone.
Four non-earnings 8-Ks in five weeks — bylaws changes, Reg FD, director departure — suggest organizational churn that may keep sentiment cautious despite a benign +0.5% earnings reaction.
Flat -0.4% earnings reaction and a routine director filing offer no clear sentiment signal in either direction.
A solid +2.5% earnings reaction and quiet filing cadence since suggest positive tone is intact without being crowded.
Flat earnings reaction (-0.3%) and a high volume of governance/other filings create noise without a clear directional sentiment shift.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 68% in Three Months While Markets Remain Complacent—Geopolitical Risk Mispriced
memos.body: I am struck by the stark divergence between the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index at 524.45—up 57.6% over one month and 68.2% over three months—and a VIX sitting at just 14.85, down 14% month-over-month. This gap suggests markets are not pricing the structural policy risks I see building, whether from trade/tariff escalation, export controls, or energy security shifts. WTI crude at $57.76, down nearly 8% over three months, signals weakening global demand expectations or supply normalization, which benefits consumers but pressures energy producers. High-yield spreads at 2.88% remain tight, confirming credit markets share the VIX's complacency rather than the uncertainty index's alarm. I have highest conviction that names with heavy China/export-control exposure (NVDA) and global capex sensitivity (CAT) face the most geopolitical headwind, while domestically oriented defensives (PG, UNH) and diversified tech platforms (MSFT) are better positioned until policy clarity emerges.

views.note: Semiconductor export controls to China remain the single largest structural geopolitical risk in the universe; the 68% surge in policy uncertainty reinforces that further restrictions are plausible.
Global capex-sensitive name faces headwinds from elevated trade-policy uncertainty and weakening demand signals embedded in falling crude prices.
WTI at $57.76 and falling 8% over three months pressures upstream margins, but multiple recent 8-K filings suggest active portfolio management; energy security policy could swing either way.
Domestically oriented consumer staple with defensive characteristics is well-positioned when policy uncertainty is elevated and credit spreads remain benign.
Diversified cloud and enterprise software revenue is less exposed to export-control risk than hardware peers; policy uncertainty favors recurring-revenue models.

Domestic healthcare services face regulatory rather than geopolitical risk; elevated policy uncertainty index warrants monitoring for Medicare/Medicaid policy shifts, but trade-war exposure is minimal.
Steepening yield curve (+13bp over 3m) supports NII, but a policy-uncertainty spike of this magnitude historically precedes credit-quality deterioration; watching HY spreads for confirmation.

Macro analyst is only neutral but not negative. Highest-conviction position.
